title: Quantization-induced failure correlation: do quantized variants of a model break identically?

original_idea.body:
# Quantization-induced failure correlation

Take one open model at full/8-bit/4-bit precision; on an error-prone prompt set, test whether failures are shared across precisions vs introduced independently. Repeat for a second family. Public quantized checkpoints; inference only.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 3: plausible chain (precision axis gives illusory diversity) but the catastrophic-risk link is weak.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: run full/8-bit/4-bit on prompts and compare failures; standard tooling, beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped single comparison (failure overlap across precisions) with clear criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public quantized checkpoints, deployer-relevant, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Quantized models run easily on a single consumer GPU; inference only.

novelty.reasoning: Quantization degradation studied; the correlated-failure-across-precisions framing may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Quantization effects studied; correlated-failure framing across precisions is plausibly open.
